description: Legal grounding for the ChildSafeAds ST3 compliance flags. Severity: per_se (prohibited outright under the UCPD blacklist) / conditional (prohibited where the general clauses are met) / soft_law (codes of conduct) / none (housekeeping label). Tier-2 flags carry scored=false: bonus track, not labelled in this release.

instruments.note: Advertorial without identification; unfair, misleading and aggressive practices.
Identification requirements for audiovisual commercial communications (sponsorship, product placement); video-sharing platforms must reflect them in their terms.
Advertising-transparency duties on the platform side; protection of minors including the Art. 28 guidelines.

inadequate_disclosure.edition1_scope: Text and disclosure-mode adequacy only; visual (AD flash) and timing assessment deferred (requires video frames).

instruments.note: Misleading actions and omissions read with the vulnerable-consumer benchmark: the average member of a child audience.
Information addressed to minors must be child-friendly, age-appropriate, presented at the relevant point of use.
Direct exhortation to children to buy, or to persuade parents or other adults to buy for them. Blacklisted; highest-severity Tier-1 flag.

misleading_claim.edition1_scope: Risky-claim-type detection (characteristics, performance, results, price; health/weight/fitness/skincare/supplement claims directed at a child audience). Truth verification is out of scope for the classifier.

instruments.note: Misleading actions and omissions.
Commercial communications must not cause physical, mental or moral detriment to minors.
Sectoral instruments in the legal reference corpus; elevated severity given eating-disorder-adjacent harms.
Content restrictions on commercial communications (alcohol, tobacco).
Age verification where products pose a high risk to minors.
Member-State laws prohibiting or age-gating specific product categories.

hfss_food_marketing.edition1_scope: Obvious cases only (energy drinks, confectionery, fast food); rigorous HFSS requires nutrient profiling. Codes of conduct to be retrieved separately.

instruments.note: Codes of conduct on HFSS food marketing to children.
Backstop where the practice is also unfair or misleading.

undisclosed_synthetic_content.deferred_reason: Requires the media itself (cloned voice, deepfake detection); dataset does not redistribute video/audio. AI Act transparency obligations apply from 2 August 2026.

instruments.note: Marking AI-generated content and labelling deepfakes; prohibitions where synthetic content manipulates or exploits children's vulnerabilities.
Misleading-practice provisions.

defective_precontractual_information.data_needed: Checkout/shop pages: trader identity, total price, right of withdrawal, digital-content functionality.

instruments.note: Pre-contractual and formal requirements for distance contracts; applies to all digital transactions including those involving minors.
Where the practice is also unfair, misleading or aggressive.
Non-individually-negotiated terms creating significant imbalance are unfair and non-binding, including for minor consumers; interacts with national rules on minors' contractual capacity.

gambling_like_mechanics_at_destination.data_needed: The linked game or app's monetisation mechanics (loot boxes, gacha, mystery mechanics).

instruments.note: Paid loot boxes as economically exploitative practices.
General clauses.
Where AI-personalised reward schedules exploit children's vulnerabilities.
National precedents in the reference corpus.

unlawful_data_practices_toward_minors.data_needed: Privacy policy, account defaults, consent flows of the linked service.

instruments.note: Age of digital consent (13-16, Member-State dependent); data protection by design and default (TikTok EUR 345m, Instagram EUR 450m); legitimate-interest balancing per Meta v. Bundeskartellamt (C-252/21); EDPB position against profiling children for marketing.
Age verification where risks cannot be mitigated by less restrictive measures; 2026 preliminary findings against pornographic platforms and Meta under-13 findings as benchmark.
For video-sharing-platform destinations.

provisions: Commission Recommendation on EU-wide age verification
instruments.note: Soft-law reference.

harmful_or_addictive_design_at_destinati.data_needed: The linked app or game's engagement design (infinite scroll, streaks, variable rewards).

instruments.note: Systemic-risk assessment where the destination is a VLOP; TikTok addictive-design preliminary findings as benchmark.
Prohibited practices for AI-driven addictive design exploiting children's vulnerabilities.
Safety net covering physical and mental health of child consumers. PLD cited as context only (civil-liability layer), not a classification ground.
Manufacturers must assess risk for vulnerable consumers including children, covering physical and mental health.
Where the destination is an online marketplace; Shein and Temu proceedings as precedent.

instruments_annex.UCPD: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC — misleading and aggressive practices; Art. 5(3) vulnerable consumers; Annex I blacklist incl. points 11 (advertorial) and 28 (direct exhortation to children).
instruments_annex.CRD: Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU — pre-contractual information and formal requirements for distance contracts, applicable to all digital transactions including those involving minors.
instruments_annex.UCTD: Unfair Contract Terms Directive 93/13/EEC — non-individually-negotiated terms creating significant imbalance are unfair and non-binding.
instruments_annex.DSA: Digital Services Act (EU) 2022/2065 — Art. 25 dark patterns; Art. 26 advertising transparency; Art. 28 + Commission guidelines on the protection of minors; Arts. 34-35 systemic risk for VLOPs.
instruments_annex.AVMSD: Audiovisual Media Services Directive 2010/13/EU as amended — Arts. 9-11 commercial communications, sponsorship, product placement; Art. 9(1) protection of minors; Art. 9(4) HFSS codes of conduct; Art. 28b video-sharing platforms.
instruments_annex.GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — Art. 6 legal bases; Art. 8 age of digital consent; Art. 25 data protection by design/default; Art. 22 + Recital 38 profiling of children.
instruments_annex.AI Act: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI — Art. 5 prohibited practices exploiting children's vulnerabilities; transparency obligations incl. deepfake labelling (from 2 August 2026).
instruments_annex.GPSR: General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 — product safety incl. risk assessment for vulnerable consumers such as children.
